speaker: Doctor
text: Can you tell me if this rash is itchy, painful, or just looks different than your usual skin? Also, have you noticed any recent stress, sun exposure, or new products on your head?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap). Although the father has psoriasis and the weather triggers flares, the age (3 months), lack of itch/pain, and specific "red and scaly" description in a preemie are classic for seborrheic dermatitis rather than psoriasis.
